column3: Integration methods for solving numerically stiff systems.
Default integration method for fast and accurate computation of displacements; variable order and step size; coefficients are calculated assuming a constant step size

Stabilized Index-2 integration method that provides better error control over the velocity and acceleration terms in equations of motion; provided motion is sufficiently smooth, velocity and acceleration results are more accurate than those computed with GSTIFF or WSTIFF; significantly slower

Variable order and step size integration method; coefficients are calculated as a function of the step size; handles sudden step size changes as a result of discontinuities or abrupt events without error or loss of accuracy

Animation; D-cubed solver is used to do presentation animation only; no simulation is performed, so no results or plots are available; gravity, contact, springs, and forces cannot be used; mass and inertia values have no effect on the animation
Motion Analysis; ADAMS (MSC.Software) solver is used to return accurate results; you must load the SOLIDWORKS Motion add-in with a SOLIDWORKS premium license to use this option

Legacy COSMOSMotion; in SOLIDWORKS 2007 and earlier, motion analysis was provided through the COSMOSMotion add-in; this option is available if either the COSMOSMotion add-in is loaded or you open an older model that was created using that add-in; models with legacy COSMOSMotion data can be opened but not edited
Basic Motion; NVIDIA phys-x solver is used to perform fast and approximate dynamic analysis; quickly returns results that look realistic at the cost of accuracy
